output: A study looked at a treatment called GnRH agonist for women trying to get pregnant using a method called IVF or ICSI. They studied 165 women who got this treatment and 165 who didn't. The women who got the treatment had more chances of having a baby that could grow normally inside them. But they also had more chances of getting a baby growing inside them, even if it wasn't a healthy baby. The study found that the treatment might help increase the chances of having a baby, but the results weren't very clear because some parts of the study had too much difference between them. The study couldn't tell if the treatment would cause problems like having more than one baby or a baby growing in the wrong place. Also, the study didn't have enough information about any possible bad effects the treatment might have on the mother or the baby. So, while the treatment seems to help, we don't know for sure yet if it causes any harm.

output: In a review of 46 studies about different types of fainting spells, we looked at 40 studies about fainting caused by standing up too fast (vasovagal syncope) and 6 studies about fainting caused by touching a special spot in your neck (carotid sinus syncope). We didn't find any studies about fainting when you're scared or stressed. Most of the studies had only a few people in them, with an average of about 42 people. Some studies gave fake medicine instead of real medicine to compare it to. In some studies, both the doctors and the people taking part knew which medicine was being given, but in others, they didn’t know. The results from these studies were very different from each other. For fainting when standing up quickly, medicines like beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and anticholinergics helped less often than regular medicine. For fainting when touching the neck spot, a medicine called midodrine worked better than a fake medicine in one study. But there wasn't enough information to say if any of these medicines or another kind of machine (pacemaker) really help with fainting. We need bigger studies that look at how well the treatments work for people who use them.

output: A study looked at a vaccine for herpes zoster, which is a painful rash that can happen after chicken pox. It studied 38,546 people, mostly older adults and those who were white. The study found that the vaccine worked well in preventing herpes zoster, which is good news. But it didn't show that the vaccine helps prevent something called postherpetic neuralgia, which is pain that can last after the rash goes away. The vaccine did cause some soreness where it was given, but this went away quickly. Serious problems were very rare. While we know the vaccine works well against herpes zoster, we don't have enough proof yet that it stops postherpetic neuralgia. Still, getting the vaccine seems to be a good idea for older adults because it can help prevent the painful rash.

output:
This review looked at some studies about different ways to help keep eggs or embryos safe before they're used for having a baby. The review found that there were no new studies to add to the information from a previous review done in 2002. That earlier review mentioned seventeen studies. 

In that older review, two studies were talked about. In one study, doctors compared keeping eggs frozen (cryopreservation) with giving a medicine called human albumin through a vein. They didn't find any big differences between these two methods in how well they worked.

In another study, they compared keeping all the eggs frozen and then using them later (elective cryopreservation) with putting the eggs right away into a woman's uterus (fresh embryo transfer). Again, they didn't see any big differences in how well these worked.

The review team concluded that there isn't enough good information to say whether it's better to freeze eggs or embryos or if giving the medicine through a vein is better than freezing them. So, based on the information we have, we don't know which way is best.

output: A few small studies looked at whether a plant called Ginkgo biloba might help people with a condition called AMD, which can make it hard to see clearly. In one study, 20 people took a special kind of Ginkgo biloba twice a day for 6 months, while another group took a sugar pill instead. In the second study, 99 people took different amounts of Ginkgo biloba for 6 months. Both studies found that taking Ginkgo biloba seemed to help people's eyesight a little bit. But because these studies were small, we can't be sure if Ginkgo biloba really helps or not. The studies didn't look at whether Ginkgo biloba had any bad side effects or if it improved the overall quality of life for people with AMD. More research is needed to know if Ginkgo biloba can help prevent AMD from getting worse. Some people use Ginkgo biloba in China, Germany, and France, but we need bigger and longer studies to learn more about it.

output: This study looked at 14 different experiments involving 1071 babies. Most of these experiments were small and had some problems. When they combined all the information, they found that adding extra nutrients to breast milk helped babies grow faster while they were in the hospital. This included growing taller and having bigger heads. But we don't know if this helps babies after they leave the hospital or if it makes them healthier in the long run. The studies also didn't find that adding extra nutrients made babies more likely to get sick. One thing they did find was that babies who got the extra nutrient milk didn't have a higher chance of getting a serious stomach problem called necrotizing enterocolitis. However, there wasn't enough information to say for sure if this extra milk helped babies in other ways or if it caused any problems. Overall, the evidence isn't very strong, so we can't be completely sure about the benefits or risks of giving preterm babies extra nutrient milk.

This study looked at 12 different groups of people who took part in family-based programs to help prevent alcohol misuse. Not all of the studies did a good job explaining how they picked which people got which program, so it's hard to know if the results are really due to the programs or just chance. About half of the studies had enough information to show if the programs worked, but for some studies, we weren't sure if the results were real. 

Nine out of the twelve studies showed that the family programs seemed to work a little bit, helping people reduce their drinking over time. But four of those studies focused only on girls, and one study with fewer people didn't show a clear effect. Two bigger studies with more people didn't find any difference in drinking habits after the family programs.

Overall, the studies suggest that family-based prevention programs might be helpful, but the effects are small and not always clear. They seem to work a bit over time, but more research is needed to be sure.

output: This review looked at three studies to see if a type of medicine called TCHP helps people with chest pain called angina. One study found that TCHP might help more with chest pain than another medicine called nitrates, but it only had a few people in it. Two other studies said that some people got sick while taking the medicine, but they didn't give details about who got sick or why. Because there aren't many studies and the ones that do exist have small groups of people, we don't know if TCHP really works well for angina. We also don't know if it's safe. More high-quality studies are needed to learn more about whether TCHP is helpful and safe for people with angina. So, it's best to use TCHP with care until we have more information.

output: A study looked at whether a hepatitis B vaccine works well for people who have HIV. The study had 26 people who were already getting medicine to help their HIV. They gave some people the vaccine and others a pretend medicine (placebo) for three years. After 12 months, everyone got good responses to the vaccine, and there were no bad reactions. But when the people stopped taking their HIV medicine, their bodies didn't keep responding to the vaccine anymore. The study was small and only done in places where lots of money is available. Because it was small and in a different place than where most people need this vaccine, we don’t know if it works well for everyone with HIV. We also don’t know if it’s dangerous. More studies are needed to see if the vaccine works over a longer time and if it’s safe for people with HIV, especially those still taking their HIV medicine. Researchers also want to try different ways of giving the vaccine.

This study looked at four small groups of people who had naso-enteral feeding tubes put in their bodies. Each group got a medicine called metoclopramide, but some groups also got a sugar pill (placebo) or nothing at all. The medicine was given in different amounts - sometimes 10 milligrams and sometimes 20 milligrams. The goal was to see if the medicine helped doctors put the feeding tubes in more easily.

The study found that metoclopramide didn't help make putting the tubes in any easier than just using a sugar pill or doing nothing. Even when the medicine was given in higher doses, it still didn't seem to work better.

There were only four groups studied, and they were quite small. Because of this, the researchers aren't very sure about their findings. They think that bigger studies might need to be done to confirm whether metoclopramide really doesn't help with putting these tubes in.

Since the medicine didn't seem to work well in these studies, it's unlikely that more studies will be done on this topic. But the researchers suggest that larger, better-designed studies would be needed to be really sure about what happens when metoclopramide is used.

This study looked at nine studies involving 3519 patients to see if having heart bypass surgery (CABG) or putting stents in their arteries was better. Four studies looked at patients with problems in more than one artery, and five studied those with just one problem. Some studies looked at how well people did after a year, while others went up to three years.

The researchers didn't find a clear difference in how long people lived or had heart attacks when comparing CABG to stenting. But they did notice that CABG seemed to help people have fewer heart-related problems overall. This happened more so in the first year, but it continued into the third year too. 

In the first year, people who had CABG were about half as likely to have another heart problem or need another operation compared to those who got stents. By the third year, this chance was even smaller, about one-fifth as likely. Also, CABG helped prevent a condition called binary restenosis, which happens when the artery heals poorly after a stent is put in, especially in patients with just one artery problem.

While CABG seems to be better, the studies weren't perfect because they didn't follow people for very long, and some of the patients might not have been exactly like the ones in the studies. More research looking at real patients might help figure out who would do best with each type of treatment.

output: This study looked at 23 carefully chosen groups of people who took omega-3 fatty acids for about 8.9 weeks. They gave each person about 3.5 grams of omega-3s every day. None of the studies looked at serious health problems like heart attacks or deaths. The study found that people taking omega-3s had lower triglycerides (a type of fat in the blood) by about 0.45 mmol/L, which is a big drop. Their VLDL cholesterol (another type of fat in the blood) also went down by about 0.07 mmol/L. However, their LDL cholesterol (often called "bad" cholesterol) went up by about 0.11 mmol/L. There was no change in other types of cholesterol, blood sugar, or how much people weighed. The study didn't find that omega-3s helped with blood sugar control or insulin levels. The study also didn't find any bad side effects from taking omega-3s. While omega-3s seem to help with some fats in the blood, more studies are needed to see if they help prevent heart problems or deaths.

output: This review looked at three studies with 130 people to see if two medicines, chlorpromazine and penfluridol, worked better for some health problems. In the short run, there wasn't much difference between the two medicines when it came to people needing to go to the hospital. For something called akathisia, which makes people feel restless, there also didn't seem to be a big difference. Many people left the studies early, about half from each group. But fewer people needed extra medicine to help with shaking hands and feet in the chlorpromazine group. The studies didn't show much change in how people felt overall or in their minds. There were no deaths mentioned. The studies were small and not very detailed, so we can't be sure about how well these medicines work. We know they have similar side effects. Penfluridol might be better because you only need to take it once a week. More studies are needed to be really sure about these medicines.

output: This study looked at a special kind of help called Community Mental Health Teams (CMHTs) for people who need extra support for their mental health. They found that CMHTs didn't make it more likely for people to die by suicide or in suspicious ways. Fewer people left the study early when they got CMHT help. More people in the CMHT group said they liked the services they received. There were also fewer times when people had to go to the hospital because of mental health issues. However, there wasn't enough proof to say that CMHTs were better at helping people avoid going to the emergency room or getting help from other doctors or social workers. While CMHTs seem to make people happier with their care and help them stay out of the hospital, the study isn't very strong. This means that while CMHTs might be good, we don't have enough information to know for sure if they're really better than just regular care. But since moving towards community care is so important, it's worth looking into further.

A review of nine studies, which included 7960 women, found that some ways to help people get a type of birth control called an IUD were more successful. These studies looked at different ways to talk to women about getting an IUD, like having community workers or doctors give advice during pregnancy or after giving birth. 

Three studies showed that when community workers gave advice, more women got the IUD. This was especially true if they got extra help (Peto OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.40 to 2.85). Two other studies found that when doctors talked to women about birth control during their first visit after giving birth, more women chose the IUD (Peto OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.39 to 3.91). One study found that when doctors visited new mothers at home, more women chose the IUD (Peto OR 5.73, 95% CI 3.59 to 9.15).

However, some studies didn't show a clear difference. One study about visiting new mothers at home and two studies about helping women make decisions after an abortion didn't find a big change.

Since the IUD is very good at preventing babies from being born, doctors who help people plan their families might want to try these ways to help more women choose it. But we need to think about whether these ways are worth the money too.

output: This study looked at 8 different groups of people who had a bad flare-up of their chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which is a lung condition. In 7 out of 10 cases, fewer people who got help at home instead of in the hospital came back to the hospital within a month. This was a small but important finding. There was also a hint that fewer people died if they stayed at home, but this wasn't strong enough to be sure. The study suggests that some people with these flare-ups might do better staying at home with help from nurses. It's not clear if this helps with other things like how well they feel or how much trouble their lungs have doing everyday tasks. The evidence for these other things isn't very strong. So, while it seems like staying at home might be good for coming back to the hospital less often, we're not completely sure about all the other possible benefits.

output: This study looked at one group of 64 women who had breast cancer surgery. They wanted to know if having their new breast made right away (immediate reconstruction) or waiting longer (delayed reconstruction) or not having it done at all (no reconstruction) would make them feel better mentally after the surgery. But the study wasn't perfect because it might have some mistakes. It didn't talk much about whether the new breasts caused health problems or helped people feel more comfortable with their bodies. The study found that right away making the new breast seemed to help people feel less worried about their mental health for a few months after the surgery. However, since the study wasn't very strong and might have some errors, we can't be sure about these findings. Right now, doctors don't have enough information to decide which way is best for everyone. They should use advice from experts instead. Even though it's hard to do studies like this, doctors need to do more research to find out which way is really better for patients. In the future, we might look at other types of studies to learn more.

In a study looking at different ways to help wounds heal faster, researchers found some good news and some questions. They looked at nine studies with a total of 489 people. Only one study was done very carefully, so we can trust its results the most.

A study looked at two groups of people with breathing problems called bronchiectasis. One group got a special shot against some germs that can cause lung infections, while the other group only got a shot against the flu. The group that got the special shot had fewer times when their lungs got really sick from these germs. This happened about 6 out of every 10 people who got the special shot. But there wasn't much change in how many times they got pneumonia, which is a serious lung infection. No one knows if getting the shot helps stop the lungs from getting worse over time.

Another study found that kids with bronchiectasis who got the special shot had less of the germ that causes pneumonia in their spit. But this didn't mean the kids got better or that the shot helped them feel better.

Right now, there's not enough strong proof to say everyone with bronchiectasis should get this shot. But doctors think it might help. More studies are needed to find out if it works and how often people need to get the shot. Since we don't know exactly how often the shot should be given, doctors follow the advice from their own country about when to give it.

This study looked at 46 big tests that compared how well different types of medicines called ARBs work to lower blood pressure. These tests involved 13,451 people who had high blood pressure. The medicines were given in different amounts to see if any amount worked better than others.

The results showed that none of the ARBs worked much better or worse than the others. When people took one-eighth or one-quarter of the highest amount allowed, their blood pressure went down by about 60 to 70%. When they took half of the highest amount, it went down by about 80%. Taking even more than the highest amount didn’t make a noticeable difference.

Because some of the biggest studies might have included only the ones that showed positive results, we can't be sure these are the best estimates. However, based on the largest studies, taking ARBs helps lower blood pressure by about 8 points for systolic (the top number) and 5 points for diastolic (the bottom number) when measured right after taking the medicine. This is a small decrease in blood pressure.

Starting with the lowest amount of ARBs works just as well as starting with the highest amount. But most of the blood pressure lowering happens when you start with the lowest amount. The study couldn’t tell us much about any bad side effects from these medicines because the tests were short and not all the studies reported on them.

This study looked at three small groups of people who had their shoulders fixed after they got hurt. These people were mostly young men who play sports. The groups were given different types of surgery to fix the problem: some had a type called arthroscopic surgery, and others had open surgery. They wanted to see if one type was better than the other.

output: We looked at 23 different studies to see if training before someone gets their motorcycle license helps prevent accidents, injuries, or breaking traffic rules. These studies included things like riding classes that are required and those that aren't. Some studies had problems because they weren't done very well. They didn't always make sure that other factors weren't affecting the results. Also, many of the studies had small groups of people and didn't follow them long enough after the training. Because the studies weren't very good, we couldn't say for sure if training helps or not. Some studies suggested that making training a requirement might actually make it harder for people to get their license, which could mean fewer people learn to ride safely. We're not sure what kind of training works best, but we know that some kind of training is probably needed to help riders stay safe. So, more careful research is needed to figure out the best way to train people to ride motorcycles safely.

But they didn't find any big differences in other things like how long it took to feel better after the surgery or if they needed to go back to the hospital.

Overall, this study suggests that subtotal hysterectomy doesn't seem to give better results for things like peeing, pooping, or having sex than total hysterectomy. And it seems that more women might have bleeding again after their periods with the subtotal hysterectomy.

This study looked at ten trials with 544 people who had sudden asthma attacks. Seven of those trials were for grown-ups, and three were just for kids. Three of the trials were considered very good. They measured how well people's lungs worked after using a special mixture of air called heliox for 15 to 60 minutes.

When they put all the information together, they didn't see much difference between the groups. Some people's lung function improved, but it wasn't clear if this happened because of the heliox or just by chance. The improvement was seen mostly in people whose lungs already weren't working very well before.

The study also found that heliox didn't make it less likely for people to need to go to the hospital. But there wasn't enough information to know if it helped everyone with asthma.

Overall, the current evidence doesn't show that heliox should be used for all people with sudden asthma attacks. It seems to help some people with really bad asthma, but we need more research to be sure. Until then, doctors don't usually use heliox as part of the first treatment for asthma attacks. However, the study suggests that heliox might be helpful for people with very bad breathing problems. So while we're not sure yet, it's something doctors might consider for some patients.

output: A study looked at seven different experiments involving 1919 people who play sports regularly. These studies mostly involved young adults. Some of the studies weren't done very well, like not keeping everything perfectly balanced or not having enough information about the results. Four of the studies looked at ways to stop hamstring injuries, which are common in sports. Two of these studies found that doing special exercises to strengthen the hamstrings didn't help prevent injuries. Another two studies also found no benefit. One study suggested that using hands-on treatment might help, but the results weren't strong enough to be sure. Other studies didn't find any clear way to prevent hamstring injuries. Overall, there isn't enough good evidence from these studies to know if there are effective ways to stop hamstring injuries in people who play sports. More research is needed to confirm whether hands-on treatment might work.

output: This study looked at four groups of people who got dental work done. In total, 1270 people were studied, but some couldn't be followed up with. All the studies had some problems that made it hard to trust their results. The study found that when people used something called a rubber dam while getting a type of filling called a composite restoration for a special area of their teeth, the fillings stayed in better for six months. This happened more often than when they used another material called a cotton roll. They also found that using the rubber dam might make the treatment faster for kids getting a specific kind of filling in their back teeth. However, the studies didn't talk about if there were any bad side effects or how much it cost. They also didn't look at how well the fillings looked after being put in. The information we have is not very strong because it comes from just a few small studies. More research is needed to see if using a rubber dam helps with all kinds of dental work.

output: This research looked at six studies with almost 450 patients to see if a special device called SCS helped save limbs and reduce pain better than just resting the injured part. Most of the studies were done well. After a year, more people had their limbs saved when they got the SCS device. They also had less pain and needed fewer medicines for pain. More people in the SCS group could walk around normally too. But there were some small problems like the device not working properly or needing to be fixed again. Also, there was a tiny chance of getting an infection. The SCS cost a bit more money, about €7900 more over two years. So while it helps save limbs and reduces pain, it might cause some small issues and cost extra money. Overall, the research suggests that SCS might be better than just resting the injured part, but you should talk to your doctor to decide what’s best for you.

This study looked at 40 studies with 1717 people to see if taking one kind of medicine or a mix of medicines helps people breathe better. Most of the studies weren't very good, so we can't be sure about the results. Overall, people who took the mix of medicines seemed to have better breathing, but this isn't very strong evidence because the studies weren't great. However, when only looking at four studies where people didn’t take any medicine as a control, there wasn’t any difference in how well they breathed. 

The studies didn’t find any difference in how long it took for people to get sick again or how their lives were affected by the sickness. They also didn’t look at how much weight people lost or if they had any bad side effects from the medicines. 

When comparing different mixes of medicines, there wasn’t any clear winner. The studies also didn’t compare which way the medicines were given—by mouth, through a vein, or as a mist—and didn’t find any differences. 

Overall, the studies couldn’t tell us which type of medicine works best or if giving the medicine through a vein is better than giving it as a mist or by mouth. We still don’t know why some people don’t get better even when they take the right medicine. More research is needed to understand this better.

output: This research looked at two studies that tested a special treatment called in vitro maturation (IVM) for women who have trouble getting pregnant. These studies were not perfect because it was hard to know if they were done fairly. The studies found that using IVM might help more women get pregnant than using another method called in vitro fertilization (IVF), but the difference wasn't very big. Neither study had information about a problem called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), which can happen during some fertility treatments. Sadly, there's not enough good evidence right now to tell doctors exactly how to use IVM for these women. More studies are being done, and we're waiting to see their results. Until then, we don't have strong proof to recommend IVM over IVF for this group of women.

output:
A study looked at 31,955 children to see if taking iron helps or hurts getting sick from malaria. The results show that iron doesn't seem to make children sicker from malaria overall. This finding is very strong because it's based on many studies and has a wide range of numbers that all point to the same conclusion.

However, the story changes a bit depending on where the children live. If there are ways to prevent and treat malaria, giving iron to children seems to help them get less malaria. But if there aren't good ways to prevent and treat malaria, giving iron might actually make some children get more malaria.

The study also found that iron doesn't cause a more serious kind of malaria called severe malaria. And it didn't find any extra deaths in children who took iron.

Iron helped keep more children from becoming too tired out (that's what we mean by "anaemic"). Also, the children had slightly higher levels of a substance in their blood that tells us how well their bodies are working (that's called "haemoglobin").

Overall, if there are ways to stop malaria, giving iron to children doesn't seem to cause more malaria. And it can help children feel better. If there aren't good ways to stop malaria, giving iron might not help. But even then, it doesn't seem to cause more malaria. The best way to use iron is to give it to children without checking if they're already too tired out, as long as there are good ways to stop malaria.

This study looked at different medicines to help people with a skin condition called erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL). They checked 13 studies with a total of 445 people who had this condition. But the studies weren't very good, so they couldn't combine the results. 

Thalidomide seemed to help more than aspirin by making the skin better. Clofazimine worked better than prednisolone at stopping the skin problems from getting worse. Thalidomide also helped less when the skin problems came back. But other medicines like betamethasone, pentoxifylline, indomethacin, and levamisole didn't seem to help much.

Taking 100 mg of thalidomide each day caused fewer side effects than taking 300 mg. But taking clofazimine caused more side effects than taking prednisolone.

The studies didn't look at how well people felt or if the medicines cost too much. More research is needed with bigger groups of people, clearer rules about who gets which medicine, and using proper ways to measure how well the medicines work.

This study looked at different medicines used to help people feel better when they're sad. They compared mirtazapine to another type of medicine called tricyclic antidepressants and yet another type called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).

The study found that after two weeks, mirtazapine didn't seem to work any better than the other medicines. But after six to twelve weeks, it seemed to work a little bit better. Compared to SSRIs, mirtazapine worked better after two weeks and also after six to twelve weeks. It also worked better than a medicine called venlafaxine.

Mirtazapine made some people gain weight or feel very sleepy, but it didn't make them feel sick to their stomach or have trouble getting an erection like the other medicines sometimes do.

The study showed that mirtazapine starts working faster than SSRIs, but people taking mirtazapine and people taking other medicines had about the same number of people stop taking the medicine because they felt bad.

So, while mirtazapine might start helping sooner, it has different side effects than the other medicines. The study found these differences, but we need more information to be sure if they really matter.

output: In this study, researchers looked at 98 different studies to see how well a quick test called RADT works compared to another test called throat culture. Most of the studies weren't very good at showing how well the tests work. But when they did compare the two tests in studies where everyone got both tests, the RADT was pretty good at finding strep throat. It correctly identified it 85.6 out of every 100 times, and it didn’t falsely say someone had it 95.4 out of every 100 times. This was true even when the tests were done in different places. The EIA and OIA tests, which are similar to RADT, also worked well, but not quite as good as RADT. RADT is very good at making sure people don’t get extra medicine if they don’t need it. If you have strep throat, the RADT might miss about 43 out of every 100 cases, but it’s still better than just guessing. So, doctors can use RADT to help decide if you really have strep throat, but they’ll need to do the throat culture too to be really sure.

output: A new study was found in our review. We looked at 13 studies with 4122 people who took part in them. The studies covered from 1971 to 2011. This study found that adding a medicine called an antiplatelet to another medicine called an anticoagulant helped reduce the chance of blood clots forming and also lowered the chance of dying. Both aspirin and dipyridamole did this similarly. However, using these medicines also slightly increased the chance of bleeding. There wasn't much difference in how much bleeding happened with aspirin compared to dipyridamole. And there was no clear pattern in how bleeding risk changed over time. Lowering the amount of aspirin taken each day might help reduce the risk of bleeding. Using either aspirin or dipyridamole with anticoagulant medicine helps prevent dangerous blood clots in people with artificial heart valves. But it also increases the risk of bleeding. The studies we looked at weren't perfect, so we're not completely sure about everything they found. But overall, adding these medicines seems to be helpful.

output:
In a study looking at people with nodules in their thyroid gland, doctors tested something called calcitonin to see if it could help find a rare type of cancer called medullary thyroid cancer (MTC). They did this test on 72,368 people. Most of the tests showed no MTC, but they weren't always sure if the test was right. About 0.32% of people had MTC, which is very few.

The test worked well most of the time. It correctly said when there wasn’t MTC about 96 out of 100 times, and when it said there was MTC, it was right about 99 out of 100 times. But some of the tests didn’t check if the person really had MTC after the test, so we’re not completely sure about how good the test is.

For the test that looks at calcitonin levels once, the chances of it being correct were very high—about 99 out of 100 times. But because so few people actually have MTC, the chance that someone who tests positive will really have it is only about 8 out of 100. 

When they looked at both the first test and another test done later, the chances of the test being correct were even higher—about 98 out of 100 times. But again, because so few people have MTC, the chance that someone who tests positive will really have it is still only about 8 out of 100.

While the test seems very good, it’s hard to know if it helps people with thyroid nodules. Also, it’s not clear if doing the test regularly helps people with MTC get better. So, whether or not to do this test regularly is still a bit uncertain.

output:
A group of researchers looked at 12 studies about massage therapy for people with HIV/AIDS. They found 4 studies that were useful for their review. These studies looked at different ages of people with HIV, from kids to adults, and saw how they felt and how strong their immune system was. Some studies happened in regular communities, while others were in places where people are very sick and close to dying. The studies used different ways to measure how well people felt, like asking them if they used less medicine than usual.

The studies showed that when people got massage therapy along with other things like meditation and stress reduction, they felt better overall. They also said that people who got massage therapy had fewer problems with their immune systems, like having more healthy cells that fight off germs. But some studies didn't tell us much about whether there were any bad side effects from the massage.

There's some good news here, but it's not enough information yet to know if massage therapy really helps everyone with HIV. The studies were small and not always done very carefully. We need bigger studies to learn more about this. So right now, we can't say for sure if massage therapy works, but it might help some people feel better and keep their bodies working well. More research is needed to be sure.

But because the studies were small and had some flaws, we're not very confident in these results. It's hard to know if the older red blood cells might cause more harm. The studies didn't look at other possible bad effects like getting sick after a surgery or having other health problems. Right now, there isn't enough information to decide whether it's better to use older or newer red blood cells. So, doctors should be careful when deciding which type to use. More studies are being done, but we won't know the final answer until those studies finish.

This study looked at different ways to treat anaemia during pregnancy using iron. Many of the studies came from places where people don't have much money. These studies were small and sometimes didn't follow all the rules for doing good research. The studies used different kinds of iron and gave it in different ways, which made it hard to compare them.

One study found that taking iron pills by mouth helped prevent anaemia in pregnant women. Another study said that women who took iron pills had better blood counts than those who took nothing. But we couldn't tell if this worked better for women with more severe anaemia because the studies weren't designed to find out.

Some studies showed that giving iron shots or through a vein worked even better at improving blood counts, but these studies also had problems. They didn't look at whether these treatments helped the woman feel better or if they caused any serious side effects like blood clots or allergic reactions.

Taking iron pills every day might help prevent anaemia without causing too many stomach problems. However, getting iron shots or through a vein can make your blood count go up faster, but there's a chance it could cause other health issues like blood clots or allergic reactions.

Overall, while iron helps with anaemia, we need more good studies to know if it works best for different types of anaemia and if it has any serious side effects. We also need to see if it helps the baby grow healthy.

This review looked at six studies to see if giving a substance called lactoferrin to babies who are fed through their stomach tubes helps them get sick less often. The studies showed that giving lactoferrin might help prevent two serious problems in very small babies: getting a type of sickness called sepsis and a condition called necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), which can damage parts of the baby's tummy. However, it didn't seem to help with another problem called all-cause mortality, which means the chance of the baby dying from anything.

When the studies also gave the babies some good bacteria along with the lactoferrin, they found that this combination helped even more. It seemed to lower the chances of getting sepsis and NEC. But again, it didn't seem to affect the chance of dying.

The studies didn't find that giving lactoferrin made the babies sicker overall. They also didn't look at how well the babies did after they grew up, or if the treatment had any long-term effects on their brains.

The information we have is not very strong because it comes from just a few studies. More research is needed to learn more about the best way to give lactoferrin, what kind of lactoferrin works best, and if there are any long-term effects. But so far, it looks like giving lactoferrin might be helpful for these babies. More studies are being done now that will help us know more.

This study looked at 63 different medical trials involving 9168 people who had strokes. Most of the trials only showed information about what happened right after the medicine was given, not later. The trials had people with depression join, and they used different types and amounts of medicine called SSRIs. But many of the trials weren't done very well, so we can't be sure of their results.

The study found that SSRIs didn't seem to help people recover better after having a stroke. They didn't make people less depressed, and they didn't improve how much independence people had. However, SSRIs did slightly lower the amount of depression people felt. But there were more people getting sick from the medicine compared to when they took a sugar pill instead.

There wasn't enough information to know if SSRIs helped with other problems like seizures. One big trial called FOCUS had the biggest impact on the results. More trials are being planned, but we need to wait for those to see if the findings hold up.

Overall, the evidence suggests that SSRIs don't help people recover from strokes better. But some small studies suggest they might help a little bit. We'll need to wait for bigger, better-done trials to know for sure.

In this review, researchers looked at five studies to see if certain treatments could help people with chronic pain use less medicine called opioids. These studies involved mostly women who had different kinds of long-term pain. The studies tried different things like acupuncture, mindfulness exercises, and talking therapies to see if they helped people use less opioid medicine.

The results weren't clear. Some studies showed that people using these treatments used less opioid medicine after the treatment ended. But other studies didn't find this. Also, some studies said that people in both the treatment group and the group that didn't get the special treatment used less medicine. But it wasn't always true that the treatment group used less.

Some studies talked about whether these treatments caused problems, but others didn't mention any. The studies also looked at how much pain people had and how well they could move their bodies. They didn't find big differences in those areas either.

Overall, the studies weren't very good because they had small numbers of people in them. This makes it hard to know if these treatments really work. Right now, there isn't enough good information to say if these treatments help people with chronic pain use less opioid medicine. The results seem to be mixed - sometimes the treatment group used less medicine, and sometimes they didn't.

This study looked at 44 different groups of people who were given advice about eating healthier foods compared to those who didn't get any advice. The study involved 52 different ways that people could receive this advice. About 18,000 people took part in these studies. Most of the studies happened in the United States.

The study found that people who got advice on eating healthier had their cholesterol levels go down a little bit. Their "bad" cholesterol (LDL) went down by about 0.16 mmol/L, which is a very small change. Their "good" cholesterol (HDL) stayed the same, and their triglycerides (another type of fat in the blood) also stayed the same.

People who got the advice also had their blood pressure go down a little bit. Their systolic blood pressure (the top number) went down by about 2.61 mm Hg, and their diastolic blood pressure (the bottom number) went down by about 1.45 mm Hg. They also had less salt in their urine, which means they were taking in less salt.

The study also found that people who got the advice ate more fruits and vegetables, about 1.18 more servings per day. They also ate more fiber and less fat and saturated fat.

Two studies looked at whether this advice helped prevent heart problems. These studies showed that people who followed the advice might have had fewer heart problems, but it wasn't clear if this was true because the studies weren't perfect.

Overall, the study suggests that giving people advice about eating healthier can help lower some numbers that are important for heart health. But we don't know yet if this helps prevent heart problems for a long time.

This study looked at three small groups of people who took a special ingredient called oral resveratrol. They gave different amounts of resveratrol—10 milligrams, 150 milligrams, or 1000 milligrams each day—for about four to five weeks. The people in these groups also took a sugar pill. All the studies were done carefully, but they didn’t look at things like how long the treatment worked or if it caused any serious problems.

None of the studies said that taking resveratrol made people live longer or healthier lives. Also, there were no bad side effects reported during the study. The studies did find that resveratrol didn’t seem to help lower a number called HbA1c, which measures how well blood sugar is controlled. Taking resveratrol didn’t make blood sugar levels go up or down more than usual either. It also didn’t seem to help with something called insulin resistance, which is when the body doesn’t use insulin well.

The researchers are still looking at more studies to see if resveratrol might help people with type 2 diabetes. Right now, there isn’t enough information to know if resveratrol is good or bad for people with type 2 diabetes. More studies are needed to find out if resveratrol works and if it’s safe for people with type 2 diabetes. These studies should last longer and look at important things like how well people feel and if they stay healthy over time.

This study looked at different ways to treat people who have a flare-up of their asthma. They studied 1470 grown-ups and 470 kids. Some of the studies were better than others, and the asthma flare-ups were different in each study. 

For the medicine taken by mouth, it didn't seem to help more people go to the hospital compared to when they didn't take the medicine. But it did seem to help their breathing a little bit, making them breathe out more air in one big breath. However, there wasn't enough information to know if this helps kids or if taking extra doses might work better.

The study also looked at giving the medicine through a vein. This seemed to slightly lower the chance of needing to go to the hospital. It also helped breathing a tiny bit more in the grown-ups. But again, there wasn't enough information about how well it works for kids or if giving more medicine would help.

Overall, the study suggests that taking the medicine by mouth isn't a good idea right now for treating asthma flares. More studies are needed to see if giving the medicine through a vein could help prevent people from going to the hospital, and to find out the best way to give the medicine. We also need more studies to learn if giving extra doses to people who already take the medicine regularly would help. And bigger studies are needed to look at how well the medicine works for kids. Longer studies would be helpful to see if the medicine saves money for hospitals.

This study looked at 34 different studies with 8635 people to see how well a test called POCS works. The test helps doctors know if someone has hurt their chest or tummy. 

The test found about 74 out of every 100 people who really did have a problem, which is pretty good. But it missed about 26 out of every 100 people who didn't have a problem, so it might tell them they do. 

For adults, the test was very good at finding problems, but for kids, it wasn’t as good. It found about 78 out of 100 adults with problems, but only 63 out of 100 kids. 

When the test says someone doesn’t have a problem, it’s usually right, but it can sometimes be wrong. For kids, it misses about 118 out of 1000 who actually have a problem, and for adults, it misses about 73 out of 1000. 

The test is especially important for kids because it’s not very good at finding problems in their tummy. If the test says a kid doesn’t have a problem, the doctor should use another test like a CT scan to make sure. 

For chest problems, the test seems to work better, but more studies need to be done to be sure. Overall, the test can help doctors decide what to do next, but it shouldn’t be used alone to check for tummy problems in kids.

This research looked at a few studies involving children under eight years old who were given special medicine to prevent a type of bacteria called Staphylococcus aureus. Four studies were included, with a total of 401 children taking part. Two of these studies had some problems that made it hard to trust their results very much, while the other two did better.

The study that did the best was still not completely sure of its results. The main thing they found was that fewer children who got the special medicine had Staphylococcus aureus bacteria grow in them over time. This happened especially when the medicine was started early in life and continued until age six.

However, the medicine didn't seem to help with other things like breathing tests, eating well, going to the hospital, or getting more medicine. It also didn't seem to make a big difference in another type of bacteria called Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

The studies were short, so we don't know if the medicine works longer term. But it seems that starting the medicine early and continuing it until age six helps keep fewer children from having Staphylococcus aureus bacteria. Whether this is important for their health isn't clear yet. More research might help us understand if this trend continues over a longer time and if different types of medicine or how long they're used could change things.

This study looked at 25 different tests involving 3096 people to see if massage helps lower back pain. Most of the tests were paid for by groups that aren't trying to make money. Some tests used machines to give massage, while others used just a person's hands. It was hard to tell if the tests were fair because it’s tricky to hide who is getting the massage. The researchers think the information they found isn’t very strong because some parts of the tests weren’t fair and there wasn’t enough information. They didn’t find any big problems where people got hurt during the tests.

For sudden back pain, the study found that massage helped reduce pain a bit, but didn’t help much with how well people could move around. For ongoing back pain, massage also helped reduce pain and made people feel better, but only for a short time. When compared to other treatments, massage helped reduce pain for a longer time, but didn’t help with moving around better.

The study didn’t find any serious problems from the massage. The most common small problem was feeling a little more pain after the massage, which happened to about 1 out of every 4 people. We don’t know for sure if massage really helps with back pain. It seems to work a little bit for reducing pain, especially in the short term, but it doesn’t seem to help much with making people move around better.

This study looked at 53 reports from 50 different studies. These studies were mostly about clinical trials, but they weren't all done exactly the same way. There were 16,604 clinical trials in these studies, and each study looked at around 123 trials on average. The trials came from different places, so it made it hard to compare them all.

The researchers checked if the studies were done correctly, but they weren't sure about most of them. Only 4 out of 53 studies tried to fix problems that could make their results confusing.

They found some good news though. In 25 out of 27 things they checked, the studies that followed a set of rules called CONSORT did better. For example, when it comes to hiding who got which treatment (allocation concealment), 81% more studies that followed CONSORT rules described this well compared to those that didn't follow the rules. 

Some other areas where studies that followed CONSORT rules did better included explaining why they did the study, how big the groups were, how they picked who got which treatment, and overall how they reported their results.

Overall, the studies showed that even though many clinical trials aren't always reported very well, having a journal follow the CONSORT rules seems to help improve how trials are reported. More research is needed to see how much this helps and if journals really follow the rules.

This study looked at 2222 people who had a narrowing in their kidney arteries. They wanted to see if a procedure called balloon angioplasty could help lower their blood pressure and make them feel better. Eight different studies were reviewed, but the information wasn't always presented in the same way, so they couldn't combine all the results easily.

The studies showed that after the balloon angioplasty, people's blood pressure went down slightly, especially during the quiet part of their heartbeat (diastolic blood pressure). But there wasn't much difference in their blood pressure when they were active (systolic blood pressure).

The studies also found that people didn't need as many medicines to keep their blood pressure low after the procedure. However, the studies weren't big enough to tell if the procedure helped people's kidneys work better.

Overall, the studies didn't show that balloon angioplasty works better than just taking medicine to treat high blood pressure in people with kidney artery problems. But it did seem to help a little bit by lowering blood pressure and needing fewer medicines. The procedure was generally safe, but there were some small risks like bleeding or damage to the arteries. The studies didn't find that balloon angioplasty caused more bad things to happen to people compared to just taking medicine. So, while it might be helpful, we don't have enough information to say it's definitely better than just using medicine.

In this study, researchers looked at 40 studies involving over 140,000 women between the ages of 20 and 70. Most of the studies were done well and didn't have many biases. They compared different ways to check for something called cervical cancer. 

They found that a test called HC2 was better at finding early signs of cervical cancer (CIN 2+) compared to another common test called conventional cytology. HC2 also had a higher chance of correctly saying when there's no cancer (high specificity). 

However, HC2 led to more people getting extra tests they might not need. On the other hand, if an HPV test came back negative, it was more likely to be correct and reassure doctors that there's no cancer. But sometimes, the regular test (cytology) might say there's no cancer when there actually is, which could delay treatment.

The evidence about how good these tests are isn't perfect - it's mostly moderate quality. But we know for sure that HC2 is better at finding early signs of cervical cancer. More studies are needed to see how these tests affect real-world care and outcomes.

The good news is that these exercises seem safe for most people with HIV. But we need more studies to know for sure. We should include more people in the studies, especially women and older people, and we should look at what happens when people stop exercising. This will help us understand if these exercises really work for everyone with HIV.

Instead, they checked if the gums were still healthy by looking for things like bleeding when the teeth are probed and how much of the tooth's root is attached to the bone.

There wasn't enough information to know which way of cleaning is best. The studies also didn't check if doing more cleanings would help keep teeth healthier. More research is needed to figure out the best way to clean teeth and prevent gum disease.

output: In a study looking at many ways to check if a baby might have Down's syndrome, researchers looked at 56 studies involving 204,759 pregnancies. Most of these studies were done well. The researchers checked lots of different tests, like checking levels of certain proteins in the mother's blood. They compared different groups of tests and found that using the mother's age along with two important blood markers called PAPP-A and free beta-hCG worked really well. This group of tests could find about 7 out of every 10 babies with Down's syndrome without giving a wrong answer too often. Adding more markers didn't seem to help much. None of the tests had bad side effects for the mom. But sometimes, having a 'high risk' test result can make it slightly more likely that a baby might get sick after the test. So parents need to think carefully before deciding if they want to do more tests like amniocentesis or CVS.

This review looked at eight studies to see if taking folic acid, a type of vitamin, helps keep older people's minds sharp. Some of these studies included people who had some trouble remembering things, while others just had healthy older people. But it's hard to compare all the studies because they used different amounts of folic acid and had different ways of measuring how well people's brains worked.

For healthy older people without memory problems, the studies didn't find that folic acid helped their brains stay sharp. But for older people whose blood had too much of something called homocysteine, taking 800 mcg of folic acid every day for three years seemed to help them think better. They could remember things more easily and process information faster.

In people with memory problems like Alzheimer's, taking 1 mg of folic acid each day seemed to make them respond better to medicine that helps with memory. They also did better on tests that measure how well they can take care of themselves and how they get along with others.

Taking folic acid alone lowered the amount of homocysteine in people's blood. This is good because having too much homocysteine might be bad for the brain.

While these studies showed some benefits, there weren't many of them, so we don't know for sure if folic acid really helps everyone's brain stay sharp. More studies are needed to figure out if folic acid is helpful for older people's brains.

This study looked at 20 different medical trials involving a total of 1403 patients to see if a medicine called ICS helps prevent people from going to the hospital when they have asthma attacks. The results showed that patients taking ICS were less likely to need to go to the hospital compared to those taking a placebo. This means fewer patients had to be sent to the hospital – about 17 out of every 100 patients taking ICS, compared to about 32 out of every 100 patients taking a placebo.

The study found that ICS worked well for both children and adults. When ICS was given along with other medicines like systemic corticosteroids, it helped even more. But sometimes, the results weren't very consistent between different studies, so we can't be completely sure about everything.

Taking ICS helped improve how fast you can breathe out (peak expiratory flow) and how much air you can blow out in one big breath (forced expiratory volume in one second) after using the medicine. But not all studies looked at these things, so we don't know for sure if it makes a big difference.

There wasn't any clear evidence that ICS caused problems like shaking hands or feeling sick to your stomach. But we don't know if it works better than other medicines like systemic corticosteroids, or if it should be used instead of them.

More research is needed to figure out the best way to give ICS, how much to give, and who might benefit the most from it. It would also help if all the studies used the same ways to measure breathing and how well people feel.

This research looked at different ways to treat pain using medicine. They studied 21 groups of people who took different medicines together. Some groups took an opioid (a type of painkiller) along with other medicines like gabapentin, pregabalin, a tricyclic antidepressant, fluphenazine, an NMDA blocker, or certain topical creams. Many of these medicines work on parts of the brain and body that control feelings.

The researchers found that when they put an opioid with gabapentin or pregabalin, it helped people feel less pain. But more people dropped out of these groups because of side effects like feeling sleepy or having trouble thinking clearly. Other studies showed that taking two medicines at once might help more than just one medicine, but there weren't enough studies to know which exact combination works best.

Many doctors use more than one medicine at a time for pain, but this research suggests that we need better studies to figure out which combinations work best and which ones cause too many side effects. It's important to do more research to find the best way to combine medicines for pain relief. If new medicines come out that don't make people feel sleepy, we might be able to find even better combinations of medicines for pain.

This research looked at different ways to help people who have a problem called Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), which makes them feel dizzy when they move their head. The study included 745 adults, most of whom were women. They tried out four different methods to see which one worked best.

The Epley method, which is like a special dance for your head, helped people get rid of their dizziness much more often than a pretend method or no treatment at all. About half of the people who did the Epley method got rid of their dizziness, while only about a quarter before the study started. This happened in five out of the eleven studies.

The Epley method also made it less likely for people to have the dizziness come back. It was better at making the test that doctors use to check for BPPV show that the person doesn't have it anymore. But it wasn't better at making the test show that someone does have BPPV.

The Epley method was safer than other methods, but some people felt sick during the special dance. Also, even though the Epley method works well, BPPV often comes back after treatment.

Overall, the Epley method seems to be a good way to treat BPPV, but it might not work forever. Other methods like the Semont and Gans methods also work, but the Epley method is a bit better.

This study looked at different ways to help people stop smoking using the internet. They checked 67 studies that involved over 110,000 people. Only a few studies looked at teenagers or young adults, so we don't know much about that age group yet.

For grown-ups, eight studies showed that a special internet program helped people quit smoking more often than nothing. But five studies said it didn’t make a big difference. Five studies found that adding help through the internet made quitting easier, but the results weren’t always clear. Four studies compared internet programs with regular ones, and none showed the internet programs worked better. Seven studies compared different types of internet programs, and the ones that were more personalized seemed to work a little bit better, but the results weren’t very clear.

The studies that showed the internet programs worked better had some problems being done fairly, so we can't be totally sure they worked. Some of the studies also had differences that made it hard to compare them all.

Overall, the internet programs seem to help people quit smoking a little bit better than nothing, but not much better than other ways to help people stop smoking. We just don't have enough information about how well these work for teenagers yet.

This study looked at 10 different medical trials involving a plant called Radix Sophorae flavescentis. These trials involved 898 people who took this plant in different ways like pills, shots, or special acupuncture points. They compared it to other medicines used for a liver problem called chronic hepatitis B. The trials lasted from 1 to 12 months.

None of the trials told us about how many people died or got better or worse. Some of the trials even had problems doing things fairly, which made it hard to know if the plant helped or hurt. 

The plant seemed to help reduce the amount of a certain thing in the blood that's linked to the liver problem. But the evidence isn't very strong because the trials weren't perfect. Also, some of the money for the trials wasn't clear, which might have affected how they were done.

Because the evidence isn't very good, we shouldn't trust the idea that this plant helps much. It's important to do more studies with lots of people and make sure they're fair before we know for sure. Many people use this plant, so we need to learn more about its real effects.

This research looked at 42 studies involving 4640 women to see if acupuncture or acupressure helped with menstrual pain. Most of the studies didn't have enough information to compare them properly. 

For acupuncture, one study showed it might help reduce pain, but the results weren't consistent across all studies. This study had fewer problems in how it was done, but even then, the evidence wasn't strong. There were no reports of bad side effects from acupuncture.

For acupressure, there weren't many good studies, but some showed it might help a little bit. Again, there were no reports of bad side effects. 

Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to say for sure if acupuncture or acupressure work better than other treatments for menstrual pain. We don't know if they cause any extra problems either. The main reasons why we can't be sure are because the studies weren't always done well, the results sometimes disagreed, and we might not have seen all the studies that didn't show a benefit.

output: This research looked at eight studies with 6,615 people to see if sending messages on phones could help people show up to doctor visits. Four new studies were added to look at this. The studies showed that getting text messages increased the number of people who came to their doctor’s appointments. This happened whether they got just text messages or text messages along with letters in the mail. About 68% of people who didn’t get any reminders came to their appointments, while about 79% of those who got text messages came, and 80% of those who got phone calls came. None of the studies said there were any bad things that happened because of the reminders. Some studies found it cost less to send text messages than to make phone calls. But the studies weren’t perfect, so we can’t be totally sure about everything. More studies are needed to know if these reminders work well for everyone and if they have any downsides. We also need to know if they improve people’s health or if they make them feel safer. The studies didn’t tell us much about that. So right now, we don’t have enough good information to decide if these reminders should be used more often. We need better studies to find out.

output: This study looked at 22 new studies to see if listening to music could help people who had strokes walk better and talk more easily. They found that music might help people walk faster and their legs move longer when they walk. It also seemed to help them use their arms more quickly after a stroke. Music might make it easier for people to communicate, like talking and naming things. It might also improve how people feel about their health after having a stroke. However, the evidence isn't perfect because many of the studies had some problems. More research is needed to be sure these benefits really happen and to know exactly how much music helps. So while it looks promising, we need more studies to be confident about recommending music for everyone who has a stroke.

This research looked at different ways to teach people how to do baby resuscitation. They found that teaching with something called SFNRT seems to help people learn better. One study showed that after learning with SFNRT, people remembered more about how to do it and could do it better. Another study found that in places where babies often die soon after birth, teaching with SFNRT helped save more babies. This happened especially for the first few days after birth. But it wasn't clear if it helped babies live longer. 

SFNRT also seemed to help teams work better together during baby resuscitation. It didn't seem to make the time they spent doing it shorter, but it might have helped them do things like giving air to the baby more correctly. However, we're not sure if these extra classes really help keep people's skills sharp over time.

The research also found that using special tools to help make decisions during baby resuscitation might help people make those decisions more often and correctly. But we don't know if these tools really help people remember more about resuscitation over time.

Overall, teaching with SFNRT seems to help save more babies who are born too early or too small. More studies are needed to see if it helps babies stay healthy longer and if it helps with other problems that can happen to babies right after birth.

This study looked at 11 different studies, but we only focused on one specific study. It involved babies with a lung condition called cystic fibrosis who were very young, and it lasted until they were about 5 years old. The study compared two ways of treating lung problems: one way was to do something called bronchoalveolar lavage, which is like washing out the lungs, and the other way was to treat them based on how they felt and what tests showed. The researchers thought this study was pretty good, but they couldn't be sure because the number of bad bacteria in the lungs was lower than expected, so they didn't have enough people to see if the treatments worked better.

The study found that by age 5, there wasn't a clear advantage of using bronchoalveolar lavage over the usual treatment. Both ways helped keep the lungs healthy, but the babies had more hospital stays when they used bronchoalveolar lavage. These stays were shorter though. The study also said that the usual treatment and the new treatment worked equally well in getting rid of the bad bacteria.

Some small problems happened sometimes, like the babies having a worse cough for a little while after the treatment, but these weren't serious. The study didn't find strong proof that doing bronchoalveolar lavage is better than the usual treatment for young children with this lung condition. There's not enough information yet for older kids and adults.

output: This research looked at different medicines called antidepressants to see if they help people sleep better. They found that some medicines like paroxetine and low doses of doxepin helped people sleep better after about a month. However, there wasn't enough information to know if all antidepressants work well for sleep. Some medicines like trazodone seemed to help people sleep longer and stay asleep better, but didn't seem to make it easier to fall asleep. The medicines also had some side effects, like feeling sleepy in the morning or having dry mouth. Not many studies were done, so we don't know much about how safe these medicines are for a long time. More studies are needed to learn more about which medicines might help people sleep better and if they're safe to use.

This study looked at eight different experiments where some people got acupuncture and others didn’t. All the experiments compared these two groups. The studies involved people who had a liver condition called chronic hepatitis B. Some of the studies also included people who had another illness called tuberculosis. But most of the studies had problems that made it hard to trust the results. There weren’t enough people in the studies, and they were mostly done in one country.

None of the studies looked at whether acupuncture affects things like death, very bad side effects, or how well people feel. They did find that acupuncture might help lower a certain marker in the blood that shows the hepatitis B virus is still there. But this isn’t a perfect way to know if the virus is really gone. Also, we’re not sure if acupuncture helps with other not-so-serious side effects.

Three out of the eight studies got money from the government or hospitals. The other five studies didn’t say where their money came from. We don’t know if this could have affected the results.

The studies didn’t look at important things like whether people died or how well they felt overall. They also didn’t check if the hepatitis B virus was completely gone or if it was causing more sickness.

Overall, we’re not sure if acupuncture helps with serious side effects or if it makes the marker for the virus go down. More studies need to be done with lots of people to see if acupuncture works better than nothing for this condition. These new studies should be done by researchers who are open about where they get their money.

This study looked at different ways to teach people about being good parents before and after their baby is born. They studied 33 different programs that taught these things in places like Africa, South America, and parts of Asia. Most of the programs taught moms and sometimes dads together. The programs helped keep babies safer, especially during the first few days and weeks after they're born. They also helped more moms go to doctors before their babies are born and started feeding their babies right away. However, the programs didn't seem to help moms use special tools to stop having babies too soon. 

The programs worked well enough to save lives, but it's hard to know exactly how much better they make things because the evidence isn't very strong. Still, the programs cost less than other ways to help babies stay healthy. Overall, teaching families about being good parents seems to be a helpful way to keep babies safer in countries where money might be tight.

This research looked at nine studies with a total of 692 people to see if certain medicines called SSRIs helped reduce feelings of agitation in people with dementia who also had mental health problems. The studies showed that SSRIs worked better than a sugar pill at reducing these feelings. However, the results might have been influenced by one big study. There wasn't much information about how well these medicines worked for other types of behavior problems. 

The studies also didn't show that SSRIs caused more bad side effects than a sugar pill. Some studies found that SSRIs like citalopram might help a bit more with agitation than others, but it's hard to know because the results weren't always clear. 

Overall, the research suggests that SSRIs may help reduce agitation in people with dementia, but we need more studies to confirm this. It seems that SSRIs and another medicine called trazodone are generally safe to use, but we don't yet know if they're the best choice for everyone. More research is needed to figure out which medicines work best and if they're safe for all people with dementia.

output: This research looked at different ways to help people who are very sick and have trouble breathing. They found five studies that compared different treatments. Two studies looked at using more strict blood sugar control (called intensive insulin therapy) compared to normal blood sugar control (called conventional insulin therapy). The studies showed that people who got the stricter blood sugar control had less time on machines to help them breathe, stayed in the hospital for less time, and had lower chances of dying over a year. But they also had more times when their blood sugar went too low, which can be dangerous. Another study looked at giving people medicine to reduce swelling (called corticosteroids) compared to just a sugar pill. This study didn't find that the medicine helped people live longer or have fewer infections. A fourth study found that doing exercises early while someone is in the hospital (called early physical therapy) might help people get better faster, but the results weren't clear after looking at all the patients. One small study found that using electricity to make muscles move (called EMS) might help prevent some sickness, but the results weren't strong enough to be sure. The studies that looked at blood sugar control and exercise were big and gave us good information, but the study about EMS wasn't as strong. More research is needed to learn more about these treatments and how to use them safely.

This review looked at 106 studies that examined 16,260 eyes in total. These studies used different tests to check for a condition called glaucoma. Forty studies used a test called GDx, 18 used another called HRT, and 63 used OCT. Some of these studies compared two or three tests to see which was better. There were some concerns about the way some studies were done, like using a case-control design, which might make the results look better than they really are.

The test called Nerve Fibre Indicator did the best job of finding glaucoma. It correctly identified about 67 out of every 100 people with glaucoma and missed about 33 out of 100 people who didn't have it. For the test called Vertical Cup/Disc (C/D) ratio, it also did well, correctly identifying about 72 out of every 100 people with glaucoma and missing about 28 out of 100 people who didn't have it. The test called OCT also worked well, with similar results.

When we put all these tests together in one big picture, they all seemed to work pretty similarly. But if we use these tests to find glaucoma in 1000 people, where 200 have it, the best tests might miss about 60 people with glaucoma and wrongly tell 50 people without glaucoma that they do. If only 5 out of 100 people have glaucoma, the best tests might miss 15 people with glaucoma and wrongly tell 890 people without glaucoma that they do.

The studies had some problems, like some being paid by the companies that make the tests. Also, the results might be a bit too good because the studies used a case-control design, which isn't always perfect. We need more studies

This study looked at 27 tests comparing three types of medicine called nitrates (like nitroglycerin, isosorbide dinitrate, and nicorandil) to see if they help prevent serious problems after some surgeries. The tests involved over 8000 people who were older than 15 years old. Most of the tests used special sleep medicine before the surgery. The surgeries weren't very risky for the heart.

The tests checked if these medicines helped prevent death within 30 days after the surgery. They also looked at other health problems like chest pain, heart attacks, and heart failure. But the information wasn't always clear or consistent enough to make a good decision.

The researchers found that none of the tests showed that these medicines helped prevent death or serious heart problems. There was a little bit of information suggesting that nicorandil might help prevent something called "cardiac ischemia," which means not enough blood getting to the heart. But this wasn't strong enough evidence to be sure.

The tests sometimes showed that people who got the medicines had more heart problems, but it wasn't clear if the medicines caused these problems. Some people also had side effects like feeling dizzy or having fast heartbeat.

Overall, the study couldn't say for sure if these medicines help or hurt after non-heart surgeries. There just wasn't enough good information to know. Doctors still need to do more tests to find out if these medicines work or not.
